reading.body:
Equinix SV2 in Santa Clara is a 75,000 square foot retail colocation facility with N+1 redundancy in both power and cooling, but publishes no megawatt capacity figure. At the minimum cabinet density of 5 kW per cabinet specified on the property page, the facility could host roughly 15,000 kW or 15 MW of customer load, though this assumes customers deploy at minimum density and does not account for non-IT overhead. The actual power available to customers is not disclosed.

SV2 is part of Equinix's 12-facility Silicon Valley campus, which operator materials describe as the region's largest retail colocation footprint and serve over 10,500 customers. As a retail facility, it competes on shared infrastructure rather than dedicated campus power. California has 103 mapped data center facilities and only 11 with published megawatt figures totaling 365 MW. SV2 does not appear in that published list, placing it below the state's disclosed capacity tier.

For an AI operator deciding whether to use this facility, the absence of published power capacity is the binding constraint. The site's 75,000 square feet and redundancy tier make it suitable for colocation of smaller training clusters or inference workloads, but retail sharing of infrastructure and lack of disclosed capacity make it unsuitable for planning large dedicated AI training runs that require predictable, contiguous power. The retail model and footprint suggest SV2 serves distributed or bursty AI workloads, not the campus-scale compute buildouts that now drive grid planning.
